standard.title: Image composition and framing
standard.description: explore the effect of choices when framing an image, placement of elements in the image and salience on composition of still and moving images in texts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students identify how images extend the meaning of a text (AC9E3LA09). They have not yet examined how framing, element placement and salience are deliberate compositional choices that influence viewer response in still and moving images.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can identify framing, element placement and salience in still and moving images, explain how each compositional choice influences viewer response, and use metalanguage to describe visual techniques.

nodes.label: Framing choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe how framing choices — close-up, mid-shot, wide shot — affect what the viewer sees and feels about an image.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the framing of an image (close-up, mid or wide shot) and explain one effect the framing has on the viewer.
nodes.typical_width: Compare framing choices across a range of still and moving images, explaining how close-up frames emphasise detail and emotion, mid shots show action and relationship, and wide shots establish setting and scale.
wider: Compare how the same subject photographed with different framings creates different emotional responses, using a sequence of images
Examine how framing choices in film or television advertising position the viewer in relation to the product or character
success_criteria: Can identify the framing type of an image and link it to at least one effect on the viewer
Can explain that framing is a deliberate choice, not an accident

nodes.label: Element placement and salience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how the placement of elements within an image and the use of salience direct the viewer's attention and create meaning.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the most salient element in an image and explain one reason why the image-maker has made it stand out.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how element placement (foreground/background, centre/margin, left/right) and salience (size, colour, focus, contrast) work together to direct the viewer's attention and convey meaning across a range of images.
wider: Compare how image composition changes across different cultural contexts — for example, how First Nations Australian visual art uses composition and salience differently from Western photographic conventions
Analyse how moving images use camera movement and cut to create dynamic salience across time, compared with the fixed salience of a still image

response_modes.reason: Students often focus only on the most obvious salient element without understanding how placement creates a hierarchy of attention. Multiple varied images help build understanding of composition as a system of choices.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The interplay of framing, placement and salience is genuinely rich — especially in multimodal texts where visual and verbal systems interact. First Nations Australian visual composition is a particularly significant wider direction.
success_criteria: Can identify the most salient element in an image and give at least one technical reason (size, colour, placement) for why it stands out
Can explain how placement (foreground vs background, centre vs margin) contributes to meaning
